title: Samira's London Kitchen
story: Samira Haque left Chattogram fifteen years ago and now runs Shorshe, a small Bangladeshi restaurant in East London. She works with her head chef, Daniel, and her nephew Tanvir, who manages the dining room. Together they deal with demanding customers, food critics, rising costs and the challenge of cutting food waste.
storyBn: সামিরা হক পনেরো বছর আগে চট্টগ্রাম ছেড়েছেন, এখন পূর্ব লন্ডনে সরষে নামের একটি ছোট বাংলাদেশি রেস্তোরাঁ চালান। তাঁর সাথে কাজ করেন প্রধান শেফ ড্যানিয়েল আর ভাগ্নে তানভীর, যে ডাইনিং রুম সামলায়। একসাথে তাঁরা খুঁতখুঁতে খদ্দের, খাদ্য সমালোচক, বাড়তি খরচ আর খাবারের অপচয় কমানোর চ্যালেঞ্জ সামলান।

units.focus: Describe ongoing efforts in the restaurant up to now
units.focusBn: রেস্তোরাঁয় এখন পর্যন্ত চলমান প্রচেষ্টা বর্ণনা করা

sessions.pattern: Subject + have / has been + verb-ing (+ for / since / lately ...)
sessions.tipBn: অতীতে শুরু হয়ে এখনও চলছে এমন কাজের সময়কাল বোঝাতে have/has been + verb-ing বসে, সাথে for/since থাকে।

items.en: Samira has been running Shorshe for almost eight years, and the dining room is still full most nights.
Daniel has been experimenting with mustard oil since he first tasted Samira's fish curry.
The kitchen team has been tracking every kilo of wasted food since January.
Tanvir has been answering complaints on review sites all morning, and his patience is wearing thin.
Food prices have been climbing steadily for months, so Samira has been rethinking her menu.
A nutritionist has been advising the restaurant on how to cut down on salt without losing flavor.

sessions.tipBn: have/has-এর পরে not বসিয়ে বোঝানো হয় যে কাজটি সাম্প্রতিক সময়ে চলছে না।

items.en: Daniel hasn't been sleeping well since the famous food critic booked a table for Friday.
We haven't been ordering as much fish lately, because too much of it has been ending up in the trash.
Tanvir hasn't been taking proper breaks, and the long shifts are clearly affecting his health.
The new dessert hasn't been selling well, even though the reviews have been positive.
Samira hasn't been cooking much herself lately because she has been buried in paperwork.
None of the regular customers have been complaining about the smaller portions.

sessions.tipBn: Have/Has শুরুতে বসিয়ে জানতে চাওয়া হয় কাজটি কিছু সময় ধরে চলছে কি না।

items.en: Have you been following the online reviews since the critic's article came out?
Has Daniel been using local vegetables instead of imported ones this season?
Have the staff been separating food scraps for composting, as we agreed?
Has Tanvir been training the new waiters to explain each dish properly?
Have customers been asking for more vegetarian and gluten-free options on the menu?
Has the restaurant been losing money since the rent went up last spring?

sessions.pattern: Wh- word + have / has + subject + been + verb-ing ...?
sessions.tipBn: How long, Why, What-এর মতো প্রশ্নশব্দের পরে have/has + subject + been + verb-ing বসে।

items.en: How long has Samira been serving her grandmother's recipes to London diners?
Why have so many customers been leaving half their rice on the plate?
What have you been doing with the vegetable peels and leftover bread?
Which suppliers have we been relying on for fresh hilsa and mustard seeds?
Who has been posting those glowing reviews about our biryani on social media?
How has the team been coping with the extra orders during Ramadan?

sessions.pattern: 4–6 sentences, mostly have / has been + verb-ing with for / since.
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে বেশিরভাগ বাক্য present perfect continuous-এ থাকে এবং এখন পর্যন্ত চলমান কাজ বোঝায়।

items.title: Eight years of Shorshe
items.en: Samira has been running Shorshe since she was thirty-two. For eight years, she has been getting up at dawn to check deliveries and prepare the spice mixes herself. Lately, she has been training Daniel to take over some of this work. He has been learning quickly, but Samira still tastes every pot of dal before service. Old habits, she says, are hard to break.

items.title: Fighting food waste
items.en: For the past six months, the kitchen has been weighing its waste every night. The results have been shocking. Customers have been leaving mountains of rice, so Daniel has been serving smaller portions and offering free refills. The team has also been turning stale bread into a popular bread pudding. As a result, the restaurant has been throwing away almost forty percent less food.

items.title: Waiting for the review
items.en: Everyone at Shorshe has been feeling nervous all week. A well-known critic visited on Friday, and Tanvir has been checking the newspaper's website every hour since then. Daniel has been replaying the evening in his head, wondering whether the lamb was overcooked. Samira, meanwhile, has been reminding them that one review cannot define eight years of hard work.

units.focus: Tell the story behind the restaurant and one difficult night
units.focusBn: রেস্তোরাঁর পেছনের গল্প ও একটি কঠিন রাতের কথা বলা

sessions.pattern: Subject + had + past participle (+ before / by the time / after ...)
sessions.tipBn: অতীতের দুটি ঘটনার মধ্যে যেটি আগে ঘটেছিল, সেটি বোঝাতে had + past participle বসে।

items.en: Before she moved to London, Samira had cooked only for relatives at weddings and Eid gatherings in Chattogram.
By the time the critic arrived, Daniel had already prepared three versions of the fish curry.
The rice had burned at the bottom because someone had turned the heat up too high.
Tanvir realized that he had given table six the wrong order only after they had started eating.
Samira had saved for ten years before she finally opened her own restaurant.
After the inspectors had checked the fridges, they praised the kitchen's strict hygiene standards.

sessions.pattern: Subject + hadn't / had never + past participle ...
sessions.tipBn: অতীতের কোনো সময়ের আগে কাজটি হয়নি বোঝাতে hadn't বা had never + past participle বসে।

items.en: Daniel had never tasted fresh hilsa before he started working at Shorshe.
We hadn't ordered enough lamb, so the curry sold out before eight o'clock.
The new waiter hadn't read the allergy list, which nearly caused a serious problem.
Samira hadn't expected British diners to love bitter gourd, but it became a bestseller.
The critic hadn't finished his starter when the main course arrived, which annoyed him.
None of us had imagined that a small family restaurant could attract such long lines.

sessions.tipBn: Hadn't দিয়ে প্রশ্ন শুরু করলে বোঝায় বক্তা ধরে নিয়েছিলেন কাজটি আগেই হয়ে গিয়েছিল।

items.en: Hadn't Daniel checked the oven temperature before he put the bread in?
Hadn't we agreed to remove the dishes that nobody was ordering anymore?
Hadn't the supplier promised to deliver the fish before noon on Friday?
Hadn't Tanvir warned the customer that the beef curry was extremely spicy?
Hadn't you already eaten at Shorshe before the critic's review made it famous?
Hadn't Samira's grandmother taught her most of these recipes long before she moved abroad?

sessions.pattern: Wh- word + had + subject + past participle ...?
sessions.tipBn: প্রশ্নশব্দের পরে had, তারপর subject ও past participle বসে।

items.en: What had gone wrong in the kitchen before the critic sent back his plate?
How many kitchens had Daniel worked in before he joined Shorshe as head chef?
Why had the walk-in freezer stopped working overnight, and who had noticed it first?
Where had Samira learned to balance so many strong spices so perfectly in one dish?
Which dishes had the critic already tried by the time Samira came out to greet him?
What had customers complained about most often before Samira redesigned the menu?

sessions.pattern: 4–6 sentences, mostly had + past participle, with before / after / by the time.
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে আগের ঘটনা past perfect-এ আর পরের ঘটনা past simple-এ থাকে।

items.title: The road to London
items.en: Samira had never planned to run a restaurant. Before she left Chattogram, she had worked as a school teacher and had cooked only for family gatherings. After her husband had lost his job, she needed a way to support the family. By the time she opened Shorshe, she had spent years selling homemade curries at a weekend market. Those loyal customers became her first regular diners.

items.title: A night to forget
items.en: The critic's visit had started badly. The fish supplier had arrived two hours late, so Daniel had not had time to marinate the hilsa properly. Tanvir had seated the critic next to a noisy birthday party. By the time the main course arrived, the critic had already written several notes. Samira later admitted that she had never felt so nervous in her own kitchen.

items.title: Lessons from the past
items.en: Daniel had trained in French restaurants before he joined Shorshe. He had learned precise techniques, but he had never cooked with panch phoron or mustard paste. At first, his dishes tasted correct but lifeless. By the end of his first year, Samira had shown him how her mother tempered spices in hot oil, and his cooking had changed completely. Soon, regular customers could not tell whose curry they were eating.

units.focus: Describe how food is prepared, served and judged
units.focusBn: খাবার কীভাবে তৈরি, পরিবেশন ও মূল্যায়ন করা হয় তা বর্ণনা করা

sessions.pattern: Subject + be (is / was / has been / will be / is being) + past participle (+ by ...)
sessions.tipBn: কে কাজটি করল তার চেয়ে কাজটিই বেশি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ হলে be + past participle দিয়ে কর্মবাচ্য হয়।

items.en: All the spices are roasted and ground by hand every Monday morning.
The hilsa is flown in frozen from Bangladesh and delivered to the restaurant twice a week.
Shorshe was praised in a national newspaper for its honest, home-style cooking.
Leftover rice has been turned into crispy snacks instead of being thrown away.
Every dish will be labeled with its main allergens from next month.
The dining room is being redecorated, so dinner is being served in the garden this week.

sessions.pattern: Subject + be + not / never + past participle ...
sessions.tipBn: কর্মবাচ্যের না-বোধক বাক্যে be verb বা has/had/will-এর পরে not বা never বসে, তারপর past participle।

items.en: Artificial food coloring is never added to our curries, however bright they look.
The critic's complaint wasn't taken seriously at first, which turned out to be a mistake.
Unsold food isn't thrown out at closing time but donated to a nearby shelter.
The fish hadn't been cleaned properly, so the whole batch was sent back.
Customers won't be charged for rice refills, according to the new policy.
The recipe for Samira's famous mustard fish has never been written down.

sessions.pattern: Is / Was / Are / Were / Has ... been / Will ... be + subject + past participle ...?
sessions.tipBn: be verb বা has/will শুরুতে বসিয়ে কর্মবাচ্যের প্রশ্ন হয়, তারপর past participle আসে।

items.en: Is the yogurt for the borhani made fresh in the kitchen every morning?
Was the lamb slow-cooked for long enough, or was it rushed because of the crowd?
Has the new winter menu been tested on regular customers before its official launch?
Will the leftover curry be collected by the local food bank before we close tonight?
Were the complaints about slow service passed on to the kitchen staff last night?
Are the vegetables in this curry grown locally, or are they imported from abroad?

sessions.pattern: Could you tell me / Do you know / I was wondering + if / whether / wh- + subject + be + past participle ...
sessions.tipBn: পরোক্ষ প্রশ্নে Could you tell me বা Do you know-এর পরের অংশ সাধারণ বাক্যের ক্রমে বসে, প্রশ্নের ক্রমে নয়।

items.en: Could you tell me whether this dish is cooked with peanuts or peanut oil?
Do you know how the mustard paste is prepared in a Bangladeshi kitchen?
I was wondering if a table for six could be reserved for Saturday evening.
Would you mind telling me when the critic's review of Shorshe will be published?
Can you find out whether the prawns were caught at sea or raised on a farm?
I'd like to know how much food is thrown away here every week.

sessions.pattern: 4–6 sentences, mostly passive: is / are / was / has been + past participle.
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে কাজ কীভাবে করা হয় বা হয়েছিল তা বোঝাতে বেশিরভাগ বাক্য কর্মবাচ্যে থাকে।

items.title: From market to plate
items.en: At Shorshe, most ingredients are bought from small local farms. The fish is delivered twice a week, and it is cleaned and marinated within hours. Spices are roasted in small batches so that their aroma is not lost. Every plate is carefully checked by Daniel before it is carried to the table. Nothing is left to chance.

items.title: The review
items.en: Last Sunday, the long-awaited review was finally published. Shorshe was described as a hidden gem, and Daniel's mustard fish was singled out for special praise. The slow service was criticized, but it was noted that the restaurant had been unusually busy that night. Within hours, the article had been shared thousands of times, and every table for the next month was booked.

items.title: A second life for leftovers
items.en: Since last year, a strict waste plan has been followed in the kitchen. Vegetable peels are collected and sent to a community garden, where they are turned into compost. Day-old bread is made into pudding, and extra rice is fried with eggs for the staff meal. Any sealed, unsold food is picked up by a local charity every night. As a result, the kitchen's waste has been cut by almost half.

units.focus: Reflect on past choices and their results
units.focusBn: অতীতের সিদ্ধান্ত ও তার ফলাফল নিয়ে ভাবা

sessions.pattern: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle. / If + had + past participle, would + verb (now).
sessions.tipBn: অতীতে যা ঘটেনি তা কল্পনা করতে If + had + past participle এবং would have বসে; mixed conditional-এ ফলাফল এখনকার, তাই would + verb।

items.en: If the fish had arrived on time, Daniel would have marinated it properly.
If Samira had stayed in Chattogram, she would probably be teaching at a school now.
If we had tracked our waste earlier, we would have saved thousands of pounds.
Tanvir would have seated the critic in a quieter corner if he had recognized him.
If her grandmother had written down her recipes, Samira would have a priceless cookbook today.
If Daniel had accepted the job offer in Paris, he would be cooking French food right now.

sessions.pattern: If + hadn't + past participle, ... would / could have ... / ... wouldn't have + past participle if ...
sessions.tipBn: না-বোধক শর্তে hadn't বা wouldn't have বসে, যেমন If we hadn't ..., we wouldn't have ...।

items.en: If Tanvir hadn't checked the allergy list, a customer could have been seriously hurt.
We wouldn't have run out of rice if the supplier hadn't canceled at the last minute.
If Samira hadn't opened Shorshe, many Londoners would never have tasted real Bangladeshi home cooking.
The critic wouldn't have been so harsh if his main course hadn't arrived cold.
If Daniel hadn't learned to temper spices, his curries wouldn't taste so authentic today.
We wouldn't be struggling with high costs now if we hadn't signed such an expensive lease.

sessions.pattern: Wh- word + would + subject + have + past participle + if + had ...?
sessions.tipBn: প্রশ্নশব্দের পরে would have + past participle বসিয়ে অতীতের কাল্পনিক ফলাফল জানতে চাওয়া হয়।

items.en: What would you have done if the critic had walked out halfway through the meal?
How would the evening have gone if the fish had been delivered on time?
Where would Samira be living now if she had stayed in Bangladesh?
Which dishes would you have removed if the review had been harsh?
Who would have run the kitchen if Daniel had quit after that terrible night?
How much money would we be saving now if we had started composting years ago?

sessions.pattern: 4–6 sentences with third (If + had + past participle, would have ...) and mixed conditionals.
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে অতীতের কাল্পনিক অবস্থা ও তার ফল third ও mixed conditional দিয়ে বলা হয়।

items.title: What if the fish had arrived?
items.en: Daniel still thinks about the night of the critic's visit. If the supplier had arrived on time, he would have marinated the hilsa for the full four hours. If Tanvir had noticed the birthday party, he would have seated the critic somewhere quieter. The review might have been perfect. On the other hand, if everything had gone smoothly, Shorshe would not have learned so much from that night.

items.title: A different life
items.en: Samira sometimes wonders how her life would look if she had stayed in Chattogram. If she had kept her teaching job, she would probably be living near her parents now. She would cook for family gatherings rather than for strangers. However, if she had never moved to London, thousands of people would never have tasted her mother's recipes. She has no regrets.

items.title: Lessons in waste
items.en: When Shorshe opened, nobody measured how much food was thrown away. If the team had started tracking waste from the first day, they would have saved a great deal of money. They would also have noticed much sooner that the portions of rice were too large. If Samira had understood this earlier, the restaurant would be even more profitable today. Now she tells every new restaurant owner to measure waste from the start.
